chains.title: C228T creates a de novo ETS site bound by the GABPA/GABPB1 tetramer, driving TERT reactivation
chains.element: TERT core promoter, ~124 bp upstream of ATG (C228T site, chr5:1295113)
chains.cell_type: Glioblastoma tumour cells / glioma stem cells

links.claim: The alt (A on plus strand; C>T on the TERT minus strand) allele generates a new 5'-GGAA-3' ETS core; among ETS factors the GABPA/GABPB1 heterotetramer is selected because it uniquely requires two GGAA sites in the correct spacing (the new site plus the native ETS site ~19 bp away) and because GABPA is well expressed in glioblastoma lines; no QBiC-SELEX lookup was performed, so coverage is unverified.

The site lies inside the TERT core promoter, a compact element that controls TERT transcription initiation; gain of the ETS site converts an otherwise silent promoter into an active one with gain of H3K4me2/3 and Pol II on the mutant allele.
TERT is the direct and essentially only target of this promoter; mutant-allele-specific transcription raises TERT mRNA several-fold over the near-zero level in normal brain.
Glioblastoma cells (and melanoma, bladder urothelium) lack ALT and depend on telomerase; GABPB1L is expressed in these tumours, making the mechanism cell-type permissive.
Restored telomerase activity prevents telomere attrition and crisis, permitting unlimited proliferation and tumour progression.

predictions: Allele-specific GABPA/GABPB1 ChIP-seq signal at chr5:1295113 confined to the mutant allele
Knockdown of GABPB1L (not GABPB1S) selectively reduces TERT expression in C228T lines but not in TERT-wild-type lines
Mutating the native upstream ETS site abolishes the gain conferred by C228T in a reporter, because tetramer formation needs both sites
GABPA CRISPRi/degron reduces TERT mRNA within hours in C228T lines
falsified_if: GABPA/GABPB1 ChIP shows no allele-biased occupancy at the site in C228T-positive lines
GABPA or GABPB1L depletion leaves TERT mRNA unchanged in C228T lines
Reporter activity gained by C228T is unaffected by destroying the partner native ETS site

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of this specific base change
predictions: TERT mRNA and telomerase activity are indistinguishable between isogenic C228T-edited and parental cells
Reporter assays show no allele difference for the 228 position
Any TERT expression in mutant tumours tracks with amplification, methylation or other cis events rather than with the C228T allele
falsified_if: Isogenic knock-in of C228T into TERT-silent cells raises TERT expression and telomerase activity
Allele-specific TERT transcription from the mutant allele is demonstrated in heterozygous tumours

chains.title: The new GGAA site is bound by ETS1, which activates TERT

links.claim: ETS1 is chosen from the same GGAA-binding specificity group because it is highly expressed in glioma and melanoma and binds single GGAA sites as a monomer, not requiring a partner site; coverage not checked.
ETS1 occupancy at the new site nucleates activation of the TERT core promoter.
TERT transcription increases on the mutant allele.
ETS1 is abundant in glioblastoma and in MAPK-driven melanoma, where TERT promoter mutations are most frequent.

predictions: ETS1 ChIP-seq shows allele-specific occupancy at the mutant site; GABPA does not
ETS1 knockdown lowers TERT mRNA in C228T lines while GABPB1L knockdown does not
A single isolated GGAA site in a minimal reporter is sufficient for activation, independent of the native upstream ETS site
falsified_if: ETS1 depletion does not change TERT expression in C228T lines
ETS1 ChIP shows no signal at the TERT promoter

chains.title: A ternary complex factor (ELK4/ELK1 family) occupies the new site downstream of MAPK signalling

links.claim: Within the GGAA specificity group, ELK4 (and ELK1) are selected because TCFs are MAPK-responsive, matching the strong co-occurrence of TERT promoter mutations with BRAF/RAS-activated tumours; coverage not checked.
Phospho-ELK4 at the new ETS site converts the TERT core promoter into a MAPK-responsive element.
TERT expression becomes dependent on ERK pathway activity in mutant cells.
Glioblastoma lines with RTK/RAS pathway activation provide the required ERK input.
Sustained telomerase activity enables immortalisation and is MEK-inhibitor sensitive.

predictions: MEK inhibition sharply reduces TERT mRNA in C228T lines but not in TERT-wild-type lines
Serum stimulation acutely induces TERT from the mutant allele
falsified_if: MEK inhibition leaves mutant-allele TERT transcription intact
No ELK1/ELK4 occupancy detectable at the TERT promoter

matrix.test: Re-analyse existing GABPA, GABPB1 and ETS1 ChIP-seq from C228T-positive glioblastoma/melanoma lines for allele-specific reads at chr5:1295113

outcomes.outcome: ETS1 reads are mutant-allele biased; GABPA is not
No allele bias for any ETS factor

matrix.test: siRNA/CRISPRi knockdown of GABPB1L vs ETS1 vs ELK4, measuring TERT mRNA in C228T and wild-type lines

outcomes.outcome: GABPB1L loss selectively lowers TERT in mutant lines
ETS1 loss lowers TERT in mutant lines
ELK4 loss (or MEK inhibition) lowers TERT
No knockdown changes TERT selectively in mutant lines

matrix.test: Luciferase reporter with C228T alone vs C228T plus destruction of the native upstream ETS site

outcomes.outcome: Single site suffices and gain is serum/ERK dependent
No gain from C228T in any configuration

matrix.test: Isogenic CRISPR knock-in of C228T into a TERT-silent primary cell line; measure TERT mRNA, telomerase and telomere length

next_experiment: Mine existing GABPA/GABPB1 and ETS1 ChIP-seq datasets from C228T-heterozygous glioblastoma or melanoma lines for allele-specific reads over chr5:1295113; this costs nothing new and directly distinguishes GABP (H1) from ETS1 (H2), while absence of any allele-biased ETS occupancy would support the null.
